claim: 2'-O-rRNA methylation is essential in eukaryotes and archaea.
source: 2'-O-rRNA methylation, which is essential in eukaryotes and archaea, is catalysed by the Box C/D RNP complex in an RNA-guided manner.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the importance of 2'-O-rRNA methylation in these domains of life.

claim: 2'-O-rRNA methylation is catalysed by the Box C/D RNP complex in an RNA-guided manner.
source: 2'-O-rRNA methylation, which is essential in eukaryotes and archaea, is catalysed by the Box C/D RNP complex in an RNA-guided manner.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of 2'-O-rRNA methylation.

claim: The abundance of site-specific modifications shows variability across species and tissues despite conservation of methylation sites.
source: Despite the conservation of the methylation sites, the abundance of site-specific modifications shows variability across species and tissues, suggesting that rRNA methylation may provide a means of controlling gene expression.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the manuscript (Krogh et al., 2016) and represents an observation from the literature.

claim: rRNA methylation may provide a means of controlling gene expression.
source: Despite the conservation of the methylation sites, the abundance of site-specific modifications shows variability across species and tissues, suggesting that rRNA methylation may provide a means of controlling gene expression.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed variability in methylation levels.

claim: All Box C/D RNPs are thought to adopt a similar structure.
source: As all Box C/D RNPs are thought to adopt a similar structure, it remains unclear how the methylation efficiency is regulated.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from structural studies of Box C/D RNPs.

claim: The affinity of the catalytic module fibrillarin for the substrate–guide helix is dependent on the RNA sequence outside the methylation site in the context of the Box C/D RNP.
source: Here, we provide the first structural evidence that, in the context of the Box C/D RNP, the affinity of the catalytic module fibrillarin for the substrate–guide helix is dependent on the RNA sequence outside the methylation site, thus providing a mechanism by which both the substrate and guide RNA sequences determine the degree of methylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both the substrate and guide RNA sequences determine the degree of methylation.
source: Here, we provide the first structural evidence that, in the context of the Box C/D RNP, the affinity of the catalytic module fibrillarin for the substrate–guide helix is dependent on the RNA sequence outside the methylation site, thus providing a mechanism by which both the substrate and guide RNA sequences determine the degree of methylation.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study based on the structural and functional data.

claim: An iterative structure-calculation protocol was developed that exploits integrative structural biology to characterize conformational ensembles.
source: To reach this result, we develop an iterative structure-calculation protocol that exploits the power of integrative structural biology to characterize conformational ensembles.
evidence: This is a methodological development described in the manuscript.

claim: More than 140 chemical modifications support RNA function in all three domains of life.
source: All classes of RNA are modified, and RNA processing and editing mechanisms are highly conserved, with more than 140 chemical modifications supporting RNA function in all three domains of life (Machnicka et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Machnicka et al., 2013.

claim: 2'-O-methylation is the most abundant modification in rRNA.
source: In rRNA, the most abundant modification is 2'-O-methylation, which impacts pre-rRNA processing, ribosome assembly and function.
evidence: This is established knowledge about rRNA modifications.

claim: 2'-O-methylation impacts pre-rRNA processing, ribosome assembly and function.
source: In rRNA, the most abundant modification is 2'-O-methylation, which impacts pre-rRNA processing, ribosome assembly and function.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by the literature.

claim: 2'-O-methylation protects RNA from ribonucleolytic cleavage.
source: Functionally, 2'-O-methylation has been shown to protect RNA from ribonucleolytic cleavage (Herschlag et al., 1993), stabilize single base-pairs, act as a chaperone (Helm, 2006; Williams et al., 2001) and influence folding at high temperatures (Kawai et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Herschlag et al., 1993.

claim: 2'-O-methylation stabilizes single base-pairs.
source: Functionally, 2'-O-methylation has been shown to protect RNA from ribonucleolytic cleavage (Herschlag et al., 1993), stabilize single base-pairs, act as a chaperone (Helm, 2006; Williams et al., 2001) and influence folding at high temperatures (Kawai et al., 1992).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the literature.

claim: 2'-O-methylation acts as a chaperone.
source: Functionally, 2'-O-methylation has been shown to protect RNA from ribonucleolytic cleavage (Herschlag et al., 1993), stabilize single base-pairs, act as a chaperone (Helm, 2006; Williams et al., 2001) and influence folding at high temperatures (Kawai et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Helm, 2006 and Williams et al., 2001.

claim: 2'-O-methylation influences RNA folding at high temperatures.
source: Functionally, 2'-O-methylation has been shown to protect RNA from ribonucleolytic cleavage (Herschlag et al., 1993), stabilize single base-pairs, act as a chaperone (Helm, 2006; Williams et al., 2001) and influence folding at high temperatures (Kawai et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kawai et al., 1992.

claim: Methylation sites are largely conserved and cluster in functionally important regions of the ribosome.
source: Recent evidence shows that, while methylation sites are largely conserved and cluster in functionally important regions of the ribosome (Decatur and Fournier, 2002), the abundance of modified nucleotides is not uniform across species, or even across tissues.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Decatur and Fournier, 2002.

claim: The abundance of modified nucleotides is not uniform across species or tissues.
source: Recent evidence shows that, while methylation sites are largely conserved and cluster in functionally important regions of the ribosome (Decatur and Fournier, 2002), the abundance of modified nucleotides is not uniform across species, or even across tissues.
evidence: This is an observation from the literature.

claim: In humans, one third of methylated sites show variable levels of modification according to the cell-type.
source: In humans, one third of methylated sites show variable levels of modification according to the cell-type (Krogh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Krogh et al., 2016.

claim: The heterogeneous ribosome population resulting from different methylation levels is consistent with the notion of specialized ribosomes that translate particular genes with improved efficiency.
source: The heterogeneous ribosome population resulting from these different methylation levels is consistent with the notion of specialized ribosomes that translate particular genes with improved efficiency (Xue and Barna, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xue and Barna, 2012.

claim: In bacteria, a protein enzyme catalyses 2'-O-methylation at a handful of rRNA sites.
source: In agreement with its putative role in regulating translation, the complexity of rRNA 2'-O-methylation has increased with evolution: in bacteria, a protein enzyme catalyses 2'-O-methylation at a handful of rRNA sites, while in yeast and humans a small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein complex (the Box C/D snoRNP) uses a set of guide RNAs to deposit methyl groups in a sequence-specific manner at ~50 and 100 rRNA sites, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge about bacterial methylation mechanisms.

claim: In yeast, the Box C/D snoRNP uses guide RNAs to deposit methyl groups at ~50 rRNA sites.
source: In agreement with its putative role in regulating translation, the complexity of rRNA 2'-O-methylation has increased with evolution: in bacteria, a protein enzyme catalyses 2'-O-methylation at a handful of rRNA sites, while in yeast and humans a small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein complex (the Box C/D snoRNP) uses a set of guide RNAs to deposit methyl groups in a sequence-specific manner at ~50 and 100 rRNA sites, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge about yeast methylation.

claim: In humans, the Box C/D snoRNP uses guide RNAs to deposit methyl groups at ~100 rRNA sites.
source: In agreement with its putative role in regulating translation, the complexity of rRNA 2'-O-methylation has increased with evolution: in bacteria, a protein enzyme catalyses 2'-O-methylation at a handful of rRNA sites, while in yeast and humans a small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein complex (the Box C/D snoRNP) uses a set of guide RNAs to deposit methyl groups in a sequence-specific manner at ~50 and 100 rRNA sites, respectively.
evidence: This is established knowledge about human methylation.

claim: Box C/D RNPs are involved in rRNA processing.
source: Besides their role in guiding 2'-O-methylation, Box C/D RNPs are involved in a variety of other functions, ranging from rRNA processing (for example, the U3 snoRNP, Kass et al., 1990) to RNA base acetylation (Sharma et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kass et al., 1990.

claim: Box C/D RNPs are involved in RNA base acetylation.
source: Besides their role in guiding 2'-O-methylation, Box C/D RNPs are involved in a variety of other functions, ranging from rRNA processing (for example, the U3 snoRNP, Kass et al., 1990) to RNA base acetylation (Sharma et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sharma et al., 2017.

claim: Nearly half of all human snoRNPs have no predictable rRNA targets.
source: Furthermore, nearly half of all human snoRNPs have no predictable rRNA targets, suggesting that they may have other roles within the cell (Falaleeva et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Falaleeva et al., 2017.

claim: Some orphan snoRNPs have been associated with cancer and other diseases.
source: Some of these so-called orphan snoRNPs have been associated with cancer and other diseases (Gong et al., 2017; Williams and Farzaneh, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gong et al., 2017 and Williams and Farzaneh, 2012.

claim: The lack of an in vitro reconstitution protocol yielding an active snoRNP currently precludes mechanistic and structural studies of the eukaryotic Box C/D complex.
source: The lack of an in vitro reconstitution protocol yielding an active snoRNP currently precludes mechanistic and structural studies of the eukaryotic Box C/D complex.
evidence: This is a statement about the current limitations in the field.

claim: All structural and in vitro functional work to date has focused on the archaeal Box C/D sRNP.
source: All structural and in vitro functional work to date has focused on the archaeal Box C/D sRNP (Figure 1a).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: The validity of the archaeal system as a proxy for the eukaryotic enzyme is established by their architectural similarity and comparable complexity of rRNA methylation patterns.
source: The validity of this system as a proxy for the eukaryotic enzyme is established by their architectural similarity and comparable complexity of the rRNA methylation patterns (~115 rRNA methylation sites are predicted in Pyrococcus furiosus).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural and functional similarities.

claim: ~115 rRNA methylation sites are predicted in Pyrococcus furiosus.
source: The validity of this system as a proxy for the eukaryotic enzyme is established by their architectural similarity and comparable complexity of the rRNA methylation patterns (~115 rRNA methylation sites are predicted in Pyrococcus furiosus).
evidence: This is a quantitative prediction about P. furiosus.

claim: The apo st-sR26 RNP has an Rg of 54.3 Å, consistent with a di-RNP architecture.
source: The SAXS curves of the apo sRNP assembled with st-sR26 (Figure 1c) correspond to a radius-of-gyration (Rg) of 54.3 Å, which is consistent with a di-RNP architecture (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS data shown in Figure 1c and comparison to theoretical distributions in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Addition of 1.25 molar equivalents of substrate D' to the apo st-sR26 RNP reduces the Rg to 47.3 Å.
source: Addition of 1.25 molar equivalents of either substrate D or D' reduces the Rg from 54.3 Å to 50.0 or 47.3 Å, respectively, with a further reduction to 45.0 Å, upon addition of both substrates (holo state) (Graziadei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS measurements.

claim: Addition of 1.25 molar equivalents of substrate D to the apo st-sR26 RNP reduces the Rg to 50.0 Å.
source: Addition of 1.25 molar equivalents of either substrate D or D' reduces the Rg from 54.3 Å to 50.0 or 47.3 Å, respectively, with a further reduction to 45.0 Å, upon addition of both substrates (holo state) (Graziadei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS measurements.

claim: Addition of both substrates D and D' to the apo st-sR26 RNP reduces the Rg to 45.0 Å.
source: Addition of 1.25 molar equivalents of either substrate D or D' reduces the Rg from 54.3 Å to 50.0 or 47.3 Å, respectively, with a further reduction to 45.0 Å, upon addition of both substrates (holo state) (Graziadei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS measurements and citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: Both the half-loaded and holo st-sR26 complexes are mono-RNPs.
source: These radii are no longer compatible with a di-RNP, demonstrating that both the half-loaded and holo st-sR26 complexes are mono-RNPs (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is inferred from the Rg values and comparison to theoretical distributions.

claim: The Box C/D RNP assembled with sR26 transitions from a di-RNP to a mono-RNP upon substrate RNA binding.
source: The same transition from a di-RNP to a mono-RNP occurred for the Box C/D RNP assembled with sR26 upon substrate RNA binding (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The RNP assembled with ssR26 remained a di-RNP after saturation of the substrate RNA binding sites.
source: The RNP assembled with ssR26 remained a di-RNP after saturation of the substrate RNA binding sites (Lapinaite et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lapinaite et al., 2013.

claim: The guide sequence strongly influences the oligomerization state of the holo complex.
source: We conclude that the guide sequence strongly influences the oligomerization state of the holo complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experiments with st-sR26-1 and st-sR26-2 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: The Box C/D enzyme containing st-sR26-1 maintained the di-RNP architecture upon binding of substrate RNAs.
source: Interestingly, the Box C/D enzyme containing st-sR26-1 maintained the di-RNP architecture upon binding of either substrate RNAs, while the sRNP containing st-sR26-2 transitioned to the mono-RNP state (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: The sRNP containing st-sR26-2 transitioned to the mono-RNP state upon substrate binding.
source: Interestingly, the Box C/D enzyme containing st-sR26-1 maintained the di-RNP architecture upon binding of either substrate RNAs, while the sRNP containing st-sR26-2 transitioned to the mono-RNP state (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5b.

claim: Mutation of the last nucleotide of st-sR26-1 guide D to C or U did not perturb the di-RNP architecture.
source: Mutation of the last nucleotide of st-sR26-1 guide D to either C or U (A61C and A61U with complementary substrate D) did not perturb the di-RNP architecture (Figure 1—figure supplement 5c).
evidence: This is supported by SAXS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5c.

claim: The number and relative intensities of the maxima in the P(r) distribution are compatible with the presence of two fibrillarin copies but incompatible with four.
source: Further evidence of the monomeric state of half-loaded and holo st-sR26 complexes emerges from the P(r) distribution calculated from the SANS curve of the complexes assembled with 2H-fibrillarin in 42%:58% D2O:H2O solvent: the number and relative intensities of the maxima are compatible with the presence of two fibrillarin copies but incompatible with the presence of four (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is supported by SANS data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 6.

claim: The sRNP assembled with st-sR26 catalyses the methylation of substrate D' more efficiently than substrate D.
source: As we showed previously (Graziadei et al., 2016), the sRNP assembled with this RNA catalyses the methylation of the substrate D' more efficiently than substrate D, in a similar manner to the native Pf sR26 RNP.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: The interaction interface of the Nop5-CTD with the L7Ae–K-turn-RNA complex does not change with respect to that observed in crystal structures.
source: As in our earlier work on the fully-loaded di-RNP complex (Lapinaite et al., 2013), we started from the assumption that the interaction interface of the Nop5-CTD with the L7Ae–K-turn-RNA complex and that of the Nop5-NTD with fibrillarin do not change with respect to those observed in the respective crystal structures (Liu et al., 2007; Xue et al., 2010; Aittaleb et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an assumption validated by NMR data and supported by citations to crystal structures.

claim: The interaction interface of the Nop5-NTD with fibrillarin does not change with respect to that observed in crystal structures.
source: As in our earlier work on the fully-loaded di-RNP complex (Lapinaite et al., 2013), we started from the assumption that the interaction interface of the Nop5-CTD with the L7Ae–K-turn-RNA complex and that of the Nop5-NTD with fibrillarin do not change with respect to those observed in the respective crystal structures (Liu et al., 2007; Xue et al., 2010; Aittaleb et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an assumption validated by NMR data and supported by citations to crystal structures.

claim: The chemical shift perturbations measured for L7Ae in the Box C/D mono-RNP map to the previously described interface between L7Ae and the Nop5-CTD.
source: The chemical shift perturbations measured for L7Ae in the Box C/D mono-RNP with respect to L7Ae in the L7Ae–K-turn-sRNA complex map to the previously described interface between L7Ae and the Nop5-CTD (Xue et al., 2010; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and citation to Xue et al., 2010.

claim: The chemical-shift perturbations measured for fibrillarin in the Nop5-NTD–fibrillarin complex map to the interaction interface observed in previous crystal structures.
source: Similarly, the chemical-shift perturbations measured for fibrillarin in the Nop5-NTD–fibrillarin complex with respect to free fibrillarin map to the interaction interface observed in previous crystal structures (Aittaleb et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by NMR data and citation to Aittaleb et al., 2003.

claim: Fibrillarin interacts exclusively with the Nop5-NTD in all complexes.
source: These CSPs are conserved in the Nop5–fibrillarin complex and in the apo Box C/D mono-RNP (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), demonstrating that fibrillarin interacts exclusively with the Nop5-NTD in all complexes.
evidence: This is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: A total of 407 PREs were collected for the D-loaded mono-RNP.
source: For the D-loaded (D'-loaded) mono-RNP, we collected a total of 407 (442) PREs using spin-labels on L7Ae-Q45C, L7Ae-E58C/C68S, L7Ae-C68, Nop5-E196C, Nop5-D247C and Nop5-S343C while observing the methyl resonances of fibrillarin and on Nop5-E65C while observing the methyl resonances of L7Ae (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the data collected.

claim: A total of 442 PREs were collected for the D'-loaded mono-RNP.
source: For the D-loaded (D'-loaded) mono-RNP, we collected a total of 407 (442) PREs using spin-labels on L7Ae-Q45C, L7Ae-E58C/C68S, L7Ae-C68, Nop5-E196C, Nop5-D247C and Nop5-S343C while observing the methyl resonances of fibrillarin and on Nop5-E65C while observing the methyl resonances of L7Ae (Figure 2—figure supplement 3a).
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the data collected.

claim: The methyl-group NMR spectrum of fibrillarin in the apo RNP assembled with st-sR26 is identical to the spectrum of the RNP assembled with ssR26.
source: The methyl-group NMR spectrum of fibrillarin in the apo RNP assembled with st-sR26 is identical to the spectrum of the RNP assembled with ssR26 (Figure 2a, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: In both di-RNPs, all four fibrillarin copies are far from the RNA and their chemical shifts are independent of the RNA sequence.
source: This was expected, as in both di-RNPs all four fibrillarin copies are far from the RNA and thus their chemical shifts are independent of the RNA sequence used to assemble the complex.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural understanding of the di-RNP.

claim: Only the methyl groups of V35, I82, V110, L114, I117, V151 and V185 of fibrillarin are expected to be within 8 Å of the RNA in the RNA-bound form.
source: Methyl groups are rather sparse in the protein surfaces involved in recognition of the RNA backbone; in the RNA-bound form of fibrillarin, only the methyl groups of V35, I82, V110, L114, I117, V151 and V185 are expected to be within 8 Å of the RNA, while only V110 should be closer than 5 Å.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of fibrillarin.

claim: Only V110 of fibrillarin should be closer than 5 Å to the RNA.
source: Methyl groups are rather sparse in the protein surfaces involved in recognition of the RNA backbone; in the RNA-bound form of fibrillarin, only the methyl groups of V35, I82, V110, L114, I117, V151 and V185 are expected to be within 8 Å of the RNA, while only V110 should be closer than 5 Å.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of fibrillarin.

claim: The methyl-group NMR spectrum of the substrate-bound RNPs showed only moderate CSPs mainly localized in the spectral region containing V110, V151 and V185.
source: As expected, the methyl-group NMR spectrum of the substrate-bound RNPs showed only moderate CSPs; nonetheless, these were mainly localized in the spectral region containing V110, V151 and V185, thus confirming that fibrillarin recognizes the substrate D'–guide duplex (Figure 2a, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by NMR data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Fibrillarin recognizes the substrate D'–guide duplex.
source: As expected, the methyl-group NMR spectrum of the substrate-bound RNPs showed only moderate CSPs; nonetheless, these were mainly localized in the spectral region containing V110, V151 and V185, thus confirming that fibrillarin recognizes the substrate D'–guide duplex (Figure 2a, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by NMR data and the pattern of CSPs.

claim: The low PRE intensity-ratios observed for specific L7Ae methyl groups indicate the presence of conformers in which fibrillarin is bound to the substrate–guide duplex.
source: Thus, the low PRE intensity-ratios observed experimentally for the methyl groups of the residues marked in yellow (Figure 2b, bottom) indicates the presence of conformers in which fibrillarin is bound to the substrate–guide duplex.
evidence: This is an inference from the PRE data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The [on,off]-conformations were compatible with nearly all PRE-derived restraints (400 out of 407 for the substrate D-loaded RNP).
source: The [on,off]-conformations were compatible with nearly all PRE-derived restraints (400 out of 407 for the substrate D-loaded and 436 out of 442 for the substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively), while the [off,off]-conformations were compatible with 364 and 414 restraints for the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment of the fit to PRE data.

claim: The [on,off]-conformations were compatible with 436 out of 442 PRE-derived restraints for the substrate D'-loaded RNP.
source: The [on,off]-conformations were compatible with nearly all PRE-derived restraints (400 out of 407 for the substrate D-loaded and 436 out of 442 for the substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively), while the [off,off]-conformations were compatible with 364 and 414 restraints for the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment of the fit to PRE data.

claim: The [off,off]-conformations were compatible with 364 restraints for the substrate D-loaded RNP.
source: The [on,off]-conformations were compatible with nearly all PRE-derived restraints (400 out of 407 for the substrate D-loaded and 436 out of 442 for the substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively), while the [off,off]-conformations were compatible with 364 and 414 restraints for the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment of the fit to PRE data.

claim: The [off,off]-conformations were compatible with 414 restraints for the substrate D'-loaded RNP.
source: The [on,off]-conformations were compatible with nearly all PRE-derived restraints (400 out of 407 for the substrate D-loaded and 436 out of 442 for the substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively), while the [off,off]-conformations were compatible with 364 and 414 restraints for the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded RNP, respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative assessment of the fit to PRE data.

claim: The two final structure ensembles corresponding to the [on,off]-states are defined to a precision of better than 2.5 Å RMSD.
source: The two final structure ensembles corresponding to the [on,off]-states (Figure 3) are defined to a precision of better than 2.5 Å (root-mean-square-deviation, RMSD, of the protein Cα and RNA P atoms, excluding flexible regions).
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about the precision of the structures shown in Figure 3.

claim: The substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded complexes show reasonable similarity to the structure of the holo mono-RNP from Sulfolobus solfataricus (PDB entry 3pla).
source: When compared to the existing structure of the holo mono-RNP from Sulfolobus solfataricus (PDB entry 3pla, Lin et al., 2011), the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded complexes show a reasonable similarity (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a comparison to a known structure supported by citation to Lin et al., 2011.

claim: All major features of the substrate-bound site are conserved between the solution structures and the crystallographic structure.
source: All major features of the substrate-bound site are conserved: the RNA-guide sequences lie on the coiled-coil Nop5 domain at an angle of about 70° and the C-terminal tip of L7Ae is in proximity to the short Nop5 β-sheet 77–79 and α-helix 64–73.
evidence: This is a comparison of structural features.

claim: The solution structures differ from the crystallographic structure in many details.
source: However, the solution structures differ from the crystallographic structure in many details, demonstrating that the sRNP architecture is flexible enough to adapt to different guide- and substrate-RNAs.
evidence: This is an observation from structural comparison.

claim: The sRNP architecture is flexible enough to adapt to different guide- and substrate-RNAs.
source: However, the solution structures differ from the crystallographic structure in many details, demonstrating that the sRNP architecture is flexible enough to adapt to different guide- and substrate-RNAs.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural differences observed.

claim: Neither the [on,off]- nor the [off,off]-ensemble are able to reproduce the combination of PRE and SAS data satisfactorily for each of the substrate D- or substrate D'-loaded RNPs.
source: Importantly, neither the [on,off]- nor the [on,on]-ensemble are able to reproduce the combination of PRE and SAS data satisfactorily for each of the substrate D- or the substrate D'-loaded RNPs.
evidence: This is an assessment of the fit to experimental data.

claim: The [on,off]-structures reproduce the PRE data reasonably well for both the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded complexes.
source: In agreement with this, the [on,off]-structures of Figure 3 reproduce the PRE data reasonably well both for the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded complexes (Figure 3—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 3 and 4.

claim: The [on,off]-structures are unable to fit the 2H-Fib SANS, 2H-Fib/2H-RNA SANS and SAXS curves in a satisfactory manner.
source: However, these structures are unable to fit the 2H-Fib SANS, 2H-Fib/2H-RNA SANS and SAXS curves in a satisfactory manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: The combination of PRE and SAS data is incompatible with a single state for each of the substrate D- or substrate D'-loaded RNPs.
source: Thus, the combination of PRE and SAS data is incompatible with a single state for each of the substrate D- or substrate D'-loaded RNPs, but rather reveals the presence of conformational ensembles.
evidence: This is an inference from the inability of single structures to fit all data.

claim: The conformational equilibria present in solution are related to the position of fibrillarin.
source: Because the SAS data that are in disagreement with the [on,off]-conformations of Figure 3 all report on the position of the fibrillarin copies in the complexes, we deduced that the conformational equilibria present in solution must be related to the position of fibrillarin.
evidence: This is an inference from the analysis of which data are not fit well.

claim: The best-fit ensembles for the substrate D'-loaded sRNP contained 66 ± 8% [on,off]-conformers.
source: The resulting best-fit ensembles contained 66 ± 8% [on,off]-conformers and showed a much improved fit to both the SAXS and 2H-Fib SANS curves (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the ensemble scoring shown in Figure 4.

claim: The best-fit ensembles for the substrate D'-loaded sRNP showed a much improved fit to both the SAXS and 2H-Fib SANS curves.
source: The resulting best-fit ensembles contained 66 ± 8% [on,off]-conformers and showed a much improved fit to both the SAXS and 2H-Fib SANS curves (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The agreement between experimental and predicted PREs improved for the substrate D'-loaded sRNP ensemble.
source: The agreement between experimental and predicted PREs also improved (Figure 5).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: An acceptable fit to the experimental data requires the combination of both [on,off]- and [off,off]-conformers in the structural ensemble for the substrate D'-loaded sRNP.
source: To verify that an acceptable fit to the experimental data requires the combination of both [on,off]- and [off,off]-conformers in the structural ensemble, we repeated the ensemble scoring protocol selecting from only [on,off]- or [off,off]-conformers.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the control experiments described.

claim: The fit to the SAS curves remained unsatisfactory for ensembles containing only [on,off]- or only [off,off]-conformers of the substrate D'-loaded sRNP.
source: The fit to the SAS curves remained unsatisfactory for both these ensembles (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), with the [on,off]-ensemble yielding a poor fit to the 2H-Fib SANS curve and the [off,off]-ensemble being unable to reproduce the SAXS curve.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The proportion of fibrillarin bound to the substrate–guide duplex is lower for the mono-RNP loaded with substrate D than for that loaded with substrate D'.
source: The higher values of the PRE intensity-ratios measured for the L7Ae methyl-groups in the presence of the spin-labelled Nop5-NTD-E65C mutant in the substrate D-loaded mono-RNP as compared to the substrate D'-loaded mono-RNP indicated that the proportion of fibrillarin bound to the substrate–guide duplex is lower for the mono-RNP loaded with substrate D than for that loaded with substrate D'.
evidence: This is an inference from the PRE data.

claim: The combination of PRE and SAS data for the substrate D-loaded sRNP could not be fit with an ensemble consisting of [on,off]-conformers only.
source: Accordingly, the combination of PRE and SAS data could not be fit with an ensemble consisting of [on,off]-conformers only, as the χ2 value of the SAXS curve remained as poor as that obtained with a single [on,off]-conformer (>250) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ensembles containing only [off,off]-conformers of the substrate D-loaded sRNP failed to reproduce the PRE dataset of the complex containing spin-labelled Nop5-E65C.
source: Conversely, ensembles containing only [off,off]-conformers failed to reproduce the PRE dataset of the complex containing spin-labelled Nop5-E65C (Figure 5—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The ensemble representing the substrate D-loaded sRNP contained 34 ± 10% [on,off]-conformers.
source: When we fitted the PRE and SAS data with ensembles consisting of both [on,off]- and [off,off]-conformers, we could reproduce all experimental data satisfactorily with a population of [on,off]-conformers of 34 ± 10% (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the ensemble scoring shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: The ensemble representing the substrate D'-loaded sRNP contained a reproducibly higher proportion of conformers with fibrillarin in the [on,off]-state (66 ± 8%) than the ensemble representing the substrate D-loaded sRNP (34 ± 10%).
source: The ensemble of conformations representing the substrate D'-loaded sRNP (Figure 4) contained a reproducibly higher proportion of conformers with fibrillarin in the [on,off]-state (66 ± 8%) than did the ensemble representing the substrate D-loaded sRNP (34 ± 10%), as was expected from the stronger PRE effects induced on L7Ae by the Nop5-E65C paramagnetic tag for the substrate D'-loaded sRNP (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of the two ensembles shown in Figure 4.

claim: Fibrillarin binds more strongly to the substrate D'–guide duplex than to the substrate D–guide duplex in the context of the Box C/D RNP.
source: Thus, despite the lack of sequence-specific interactions with the RNA, fibrillarin binds more strongly to the substrate D'–guide duplex than to the substrate D–guide duplex in the context of the Box C/D RNP.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the ensemble populations.

claim: In the [off,off]-state, both half-loaded RNPs display a regular A-form helix of 11 base-pairs formed by the guide and substrate RNAs.
source: In the [off,off]-state, both half-loaded RNPs display a regular A-form helix of 11 base-pairs formed by the guide and substrate RNAs and positioned far from the Nop5 coiled-coil domains.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the calculated structures.

claim: Binding of fibrillarin pushes the substrate–guide duplex towards the Nop5 coiled-coil domain, thereby perturbing the base-pairing at the substrate 3' end.
source: Binding of fibrillarin pushes the substrate–guide duplex towards the Nop5 coiled-coil domain, thereby perturbing the base-pairing at the substrate 3' end (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a structural observation supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A substrate–guide duplex of only 10 base-pairs results in the highest level of in vitro methylation for a S. solfataricus enzyme.
source: This observation is in agreement with a recent study, reporting that a substrate–guide duplex of only 10 base-pairs results in the highest level of in vitro methylation for a S. solfataricus enzyme (Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2016.

claim: During the 150-ns MD trajectory of the D'-loaded complex, the two base-pairs at the 3' end of substrate D' are disrupted.
source: During the 150-ns MD trajectory of the D'-loaded complex, the two base-pairs at the 3' end of substrate D' are disrupted and the Nop5 α10 helix and its flanking loops form many electrostatic contacts with the RNA (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: The Nop5 α10 helix and its flanking loops form many electrostatic contacts with the RNA during the MD trajectory of the D'-loaded complex.
source: During the 150-ns MD trajectory of the D'-loaded complex, the two base-pairs at the 3' end of substrate D' are disrupted and the Nop5 α10 helix and its flanking loops form many electrostatic contacts with the RNA (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: W319 forms a face-to-face interaction with the no-longer base-paired G15 of the guide RNA in the D'-loaded complex.
source: In addition, W319 forms a face-to-face interaction with the no-longer base-paired G15 of the guide RNA.
evidence: This is a structural observation from MD simulations.

claim: In the substrate D-loaded complex, only one base-pair is melted at the 3' end of the substrate (the second last).
source: In contrast, in the substrate D-loaded complex, only one base-pair is melted at the 3' end of the substrate (the second last), fewer new contacts are formed between the protein and the RNA and some other contacts are lost during the simulation (Figures 6 and 7).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: Fewer new contacts are formed between the protein and the RNA in the substrate D-loaded complex compared to the D'-loaded complex.
source: In contrast, in the substrate D-loaded complex, only one base-pair is melted at the 3' end of the substrate (the second last), fewer new contacts are formed between the protein and the RNA and some other contacts are lost during the simulation (Figures 6 and 7).
evidence: This is a comparative observation from MD simulations.

claim: In the substrate D'-loaded complex, the A–U base-pair at the 5' end of substrate D' was often disrupted during the simulation.
source: Furthermore, in the substrate D'-loaded complex the A–U base-pair at the 5' end of substrate D' iwas often disrupted during the simulation, allowing for the formation of electrostatic contacts between E289 and A25/C5 and K290 and U4 (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: In the substrate D-loaded complex, the C–G base-pair at the 5' end of the substrate remains stable throughout the simulation.
source: Conversely, in the substrate D-loaded complex, the C–G base-pair at the 5' end of the substrate remains stable throughout the simulation (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations shown in Figure 6.

claim: High levels of methylation occur for a substrate–guide duplex length of 8–10 base pairs.
source: In agreement with our MD simulations, Yang et al. (2016) demonstrated that high levels of methylation occur for a substrate–guide duplex length of 8–10 base pairs.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2016.

claim: The stability of the fibrillarin-bound form depends on a delicate balance between entropy loss, base-pair melting, and formation of new protein–RNA contacts.
source: We conclude that the stability of the fibrillarin-bound form depends on a delicate balance between the loss of entropy due to fibrillarin localization, and the positive and negative enthalpy changes associated with base-pair melting and formation of new protein–RNA contacts, respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the MD simulations and structural analysis.

claim: The difference between the ΔG values for the [off,off]→[on,off] transition of the substrate D'- and substrate D-loaded complexes is 0.86 ± 0.55 kcal/mol.
source: we can calculate that the difference between the ΔG values for the [off,off]→[on,off] transition of the substrate D'- and substrate D-loaded complexes in the st-sR26 RNP is only 0.86 ± 0.55 kcal/mol.
evidence: This is calculated from the population ratios using thermodynamic equations.

claim: Fine differences in the stability of the substrate–guide helices may regulate the affinity of fibrillarin for the methylation site and thus the fractional population of active enzyme.
source: This small value suggests that fine differences in the stability of the substrate–guide helices may regulate the affinity of fibrillarin for the methylation site and thus the fractional population of active enzyme.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the small free energy difference calculated.

claim: rRNA methylation has been proposed to exert a regulatory function by generating a heterogeneous ribosome population with differential methylation levels.
source: However, rRNA methylation has recently been proposed to exert a regulatory function by generating an heterogeneous ribosome population with differential methylation levels (Erales et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Erales et al., 2017.

claim: The levels of methylation catalysed by sRNP complexes in vitro vary according to the substrate sequence.
source: The levels of methylation catalysed by sRNP complexes in vitro vary according to the substrate sequence.
evidence: This is an observation from in vitro studies.

claim: The efficiency of 2'-O-methylation in vitro was proposed to depend on the stability of the substrate–guide duplex and on the formation of an ideal A-form helical geometry close to the modification site.
source: In early studies the efficiency of 2'-O-methylation in vitro was proposed to depend on the stability of the substrate–guide duplex and on the formation of an ideal A-form helical geometry close to the modification site (Appel and Maxwell, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Appel and Maxwell, 2007.

claim: The Pf sR26 RNP methylates substrate D' more efficiently than substrate D.
source: Using the Pyrococcus furiosus (Pf) sR26 guide RNA, whose corresponding sRNP methylates substrate D' more efficiently than substrate D, we demonstrated that methylation levels depend on — among other factors — the nature of the first base-paired nucleotide of the substrate (Graziadei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: Methylation levels depend on the nature of the first base-paired nucleotide of the substrate.
source: Using the Pyrococcus furiosus (Pf) sR26 guide RNA, whose corresponding sRNP methylates substrate D' more efficiently than substrate D, we demonstrated that methylation levels depend on — among other factors — the nature of the first base-paired nucleotide of the substrate (Graziadei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: Substrate D', with a 5'-uridine, displays good turnover in all conditions.
source: The observation that substrate D', with a 5'-uridine, displays good turnover in all conditions, while turnover of substrate D, with a 5'-guanosine, requires binding of substrate D' (Graziadei et al., 2016), led us to suggest that the nature of the last base-pair before the box D (or box D') regulates product dissociation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: Turnover of substrate D, with a 5'-guanosine, requires binding of substrate D'.
source: The observation that substrate D', with a 5'-uridine, displays good turnover in all conditions, while turnover of substrate D, with a 5'-guanosine, requires binding of substrate D' (Graziadei et al., 2016), led us to suggest that the nature of the last base-pair before the box D (or box D') regulates product dissociation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: The nature of the last base-pair before the box D (or box D') regulates product dissociation.
source: The observation that substrate D', with a 5'-uridine, displays good turnover in all conditions, while turnover of substrate D, with a 5'-guanosine, requires binding of substrate D' (Graziadei et al., 2016), led us to suggest that the nature of the last base-pair before the box D (or box D') regulates product dissociation.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observations cited.

claim: Methylation levels in vivo do not correlate with either the number of base-pairs or the stability of the substrate–guide helix.
source: In agreement with the hypothesis that methylation levels are not exclusively dependent on the stability of the substrate–guide duplex, a recent study, which quantified site-specific rRNA methylation in two different human cell lines (Krogh et al., 2016), revealed that methylation levels in vivo do not correlate with either the number of base-pairs or the stability of the substrate–guide helix.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Krogh et al., 2016.

claim: The sequence of the substrate–guide duplex influences the affinity of fibrillarin for the substrate.
source: Here we demonstrate that the sequence of the substrate–guide duplex influences the affinity of fibrillarin for the substrate and that the extent of fibrillarin binding correlates with the efficiency of methylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The extent of fibrillarin binding correlates with the efficiency of methylation.
source: Here we demonstrate that the sequence of the substrate–guide duplex influences the affinity of fibrillarin for the substrate and that the extent of fibrillarin binding correlates with the efficiency of methylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The affinity of fibrillarin for the substrate depends on the RNA sequence beyond the methylation site in the context of the sRNP complex.
source: Using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), small angle X-ray (SAXS) and neutron (SANS) scattering data, we demonstrate that, in the context of the sRNP complex, the affinity of fibrillarin for the substrate depends on the RNA sequence beyond the methylation site.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by NMR, SAXS, and SANS data.

claim: The difference in affinity is explained by the energetics of a global conformational transition of the sRNP from an inactive to an active state.
source: This difference in affinity is explained by the energetics of a global conformational transition of the sRNP from an inactive to an active state and provides a further route, besides the modulation of product dissociation described previously (Graziadei et al., 2016), to tune RNA methylation levels.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation based on the structural and thermodynamic data.

claim: An ensemble structure-calculation method was developed that exploits the ability of integrative structural biology in solution to reveal and characterize conformational equilibria.
source: To derive these results we developed an ensemble structure-calculation method that exploits the ability of integrative structural biology in solution to reveal and characterize conformational equilibria.
evidence: This is a methodological development described in the manuscript.

claim: The copy of fibrillarin at the substrate-loaded site exchanges between the substrate-bound and unbound states.
source: Instead of a single, well-defined conformational state, we found that the copy of fibrillarin at the substrate-loaded site exchanges between the substrate-bound and unbound states, with the substrate D'-loaded complex displaying a higher population of the methylation-competent [on,off]-state than the substrate D-loaded RNP.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the structural analysis.

claim: The substrate D'-loaded complex displays a higher population of the methylation-competent [on,off]-state than the substrate D-loaded RNP.
source: Instead of a single, well-defined conformational state, we found that the copy of fibrillarin at the substrate-loaded site exchanges between the substrate-bound and unbound states, with the substrate D'-loaded complex displaying a higher population of the methylation-competent [on,off]-state than the substrate D-loaded RNP.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the ensemble analysis.

claim: The substrate D'-loaded RNP achieves higher levels of methylation than the substrate D-loaded RNP.
source: Accordingly, the substrate D'-loaded RNP achieves higher levels of methylation (Graziadei et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Graziadei et al., 2016.

claim: The existence of dynamic equilibria between substrate-bound and unbound conformers of fibrillarin has not been detected by X-ray crystallography.
source: The existence of dynamic equilibria between substrate-bound and unbound conformers of fibrillarin has not been detected by X-ray crystallography, which instead selects for the most ordered conformation.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of crystallography.

claim: The proportion of the methylation-competent complex is subtly tuned by the free-energy difference between the active [on,off]- and inactive [off,off]- conformations.
source: Our results suggest that the proportion of the methylation-competent complex is subtly tuned by the free-energy difference between the active [on,off]- and inactive [off,off]- conformations (and possibly also by the kinetics of transition, on which our structural data at equilibrium do not provide any information).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the thermodynamic analysis.

claim: Recognition of the RNA ribose by fibrillarin is accompanied by a loss in entropy at the junction between the Nop5-NTD and the Nop5 coiled-coil and between the box C/D RNA elements and the substrate–guide duplex.
source: Recognition of the RNA ribose by fibrillarin is accompanied by a loss in entropy at the junction between the Nop5-NTD and the Nop5 coiled-coil and between the box C/D (or box C'/D') RNA elements and the substrate–guide duplex.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural analysis.

claim: Upon fibrillarin binding, the substrate–guide helical structure must deviate from the ideal A-form geometry to adapt to the proteins.
source: In addition, upon fibrillarin binding, the substrate–guide helical structure must deviate from the ideal A-form geometry, in order to adapt to the proteins.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the calculated structures.

claim: Any base-pair beyond the tenth at the 3' end of the substrate is melted upon fibrillarin binding.
source: This is particularly evident at the 3' end of the substrate, where any base-pair beyond the tenth is melted (Yang et al., 2016; Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by MD simulations shown in Figure 6 and citation to Yang et al., 2016.

claim: The energetically costly events of entropy loss and base-pair melting are compensated by the formation of contacts between fibrillarin and the RNA backbone and between the Nop5-CTDs and fibrillarin and the two ends of the substrate–guide duplex.
source: These energetically costly events are compensated by the formation of contacts between fibrillarin and the RNA backbone, as well as by contacts between the Nop5-CTDs and fibrillarin and the two ends of the substrate–guide duplex.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural and MD analysis.

claim: The substrate D'–guide duplex is less stable at the substrate 3' end than the substrate D–guide duplex.
source: MD simulations showed that the substrate D'–guide duplex is less stable at the substrate 3' end than the substrate D–guide duplex, and that the melting of the last two base-pairs results in a large number of protein–RNA contacts.
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations.

claim: The melting of the last two base-pairs at the 3' end of substrate D' results in a large number of protein–RNA contacts.
source: MD simulations showed that the substrate D'–guide duplex is less stable at the substrate 3' end than the substrate D–guide duplex, and that the melting of the last two base-pairs results in a large number of protein–RNA contacts.
evidence: This is a result from MD simulations.

claim: The protein–RNA contacts formed upon melting of the last two base-pairs appear to stabilize the [on,off]-state in the substrate D'-loaded RNP.
source: These appear to stabilize the [on,off]-state in the substrate D'-loaded RNP, suggesting that the exact sequence of the 3' end segment of the substrate RNA influences the fractional population of the active conformation of the RNP.
evidence: This is an inference from the MD simulations.

claim: The exact sequence of the 3' end segment of the substrate RNA influences the fractional population of the active conformation of the RNP.
source: These appear to stabilize the [on,off]-state in the substrate D'-loaded RNP, suggesting that the exact sequence of the 3' end segment of the substrate RNA influences the fractional population of the active conformation of the RNP.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the MD results.

claim: Methylation efficiency appears to be regulated by a complex interaction network depending on the substrate rRNA sequence beyond the methylation site.
source: In conclusion, methylation efficiency appears to be regulated by a complex interaction network depending on the substrate rRNA sequence beyond the methylation site.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the study.

claim: The ability of different substrate–guide duplexes to shift the position of the equilibrium between the [off,off]- and [on,off]-state conformers modulates the level of methylation at distinct rRNA sites.
source: We propose that, together with substrate turnover (Graziadei et al., 2016), the ability of different substrate–guide duplexes to shift the position of the equilibrium between the [off,off]- and [on,off]-state conformers modulates the level of methylation at distinct rRNA sites.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the findings.

claim: When the free-energy difference between active and inactive enzyme states is large and positive, the population of the methylation-competent conformation becomes vanishingly small and the Box C/D RNP loses its capacity to catalyse methylation.
source: When the free-energy difference is large and positive, the population of the methylation-competent conformation becomes vanishingly small and the Box C/D RNP loses its capacity to catalyse methylation.
evidence: This is a speculation about extreme cases.

claim: The situation where the Box C/D RNP loses methylation capacity could be the basis for supporting functions unrelated to methylation.
source: This situation could be the basis for supporting functions of the Box C/D complexes that are unrelated to methylation and thus may not require fibrillarin to bind the RNA (for example, the U3 snoRNP, which guides the formation of the central pseudoknot in 18S rRNA).
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional implications.

claim: A novel hybrid structure-calculation protocol was developed that fits a combination of NMR and SAS data to an ensemble of conformations.
source: To calculate the structural models of the substrate D- and substrate D'-loaded RNPs we developed a novel hybrid structure-calculation protocol that fits a combination of NMR and SAS data to an ensemble of conformations.
evidence: This is a methodological development.

claim: The combination of NMR PRE data and SAS data was essential for revealing the equilibrium between RNA-bound and RNA-unbound fibrillarin states.
source: In this case, the combination of NMR PRE data and SAS data was essential for revealing the equilibrium between RNA-bound and RNA-unbound fibrillarin states.
evidence: This is a statement about the importance of the integrative approach.

claim: The computational workflow developed allows interpretation of hybrid structural data in terms of structural ensembles rather than as individual conformations.
source: The computational workflow developed here allows interpretation of hybrid structural data in terms of structural ensembles, rather than as individual conformations.
evidence: This is a statement about the capability of the method.

claim: The methodology developed is anticipated to be generally applicable to modular enzymes undergoing domain reorientation during catalysis.
source: We anticipate the methodology developed here to be generally applicable to modular enzymes undergoing domain reorientation during catalysis.
evidence: This is a speculation about the broader applicability of the method.
